articles.title: Zidane es mucho Zidane
articles.standfirst: Bet365 sitúa a Francia como principal candidata al título de la UEFA Nations League, por delante de la vigente campeona del mundo España
articles.summary: Bet365 sitúa a Francia como principal candidata al título de la UEFA Nations League, por delante de la vigente campeona del mundo España
articles.body: La UEFA Nations League 2026/27 arranca esta semana con un aliciente añadido. Hasta cinco selecciones de primer nivel afrontan la competición con nuevo seleccionador tras el Mundial de este verano. El más mediático de todos es, sin duda, Zinedine Zidane, que debuta al frente de Francia como sucesor de Didier Deschamps, y lo hace con la ambición de devolver a los 'Bleus' a la senda ganadora. Pese a tratarse de un proyecto recién estrenado, las casas de apuestas, con Bet365 a la cabeza, sitúan a Francia como principal favorita para levantar el título, a cuota 3.75. El prestigio de Zidane como entrenador, sumado al talento individual que atesora la plantilla francesa, explica que el mercado confíe en un arranque de ciclo ganador, algo que no siempre resulta sencillo cuando se produce un cambio de seleccionador tras más de una década de estabilidad bajo Deschamps. Muy cerca aparece España, a cuota 4. El combinado de Luis de la Fuente llega a esta Nations League como vigente campeona del mundo, tras coronarse este verano en EEUU, y con el añadido de haber conquistado también la pasada Eurocopa, lo que la convierte en la selección más laureada de los últimos años en el panorama internacional. Con Lamine Yamal como gran estandarte, después de otro gran arranque de temporada con el Barcelona, España aspira a aumentar su colección de títulos consecutivos. Por detrás aparecen empatadas Alemania e Inglaterra, ambas a cuota 5.5 en Bet365. El conjunto germano también estrena seleccionador, con Jürgen Klopp al mando tras su salida del Liverpool, en un proyecto que busca dejar atrás la decepcionante eliminación en dieciseisavos del pasado Mundial ante Paraguay. El carismático técnico alemán ya ha dejado su sello convocando hasta 44 jugadores para esta primera ventana. Inglaterra, por su parte, afronta una nueva etapa bajo Thomas Tuchel tras finalizar tercera en el Mundial. Por otro lado, resulta llamativo que Portugal, actual campeona de la Nations League, aparezca solo quinta en las quinielas, a cuota 9. El conjunto luso también estrena banquillo, con Jorge Jesus como sustituto de Roberto Martínez, aunque mantiene el núcleo que la llevó a conquistar el título en la pasada edición, con Cristiano Ronaldo todavía como símbolo del combinado nacional. Cierra el grupo de favoritos para las apuestas deportivas Países Bajos, a cuota 13, en el estreno de Xavi Hernández como seleccionador tras su etapa en el Barcelona. Los neerlandeses llegan con la necesidad de reaccionar tras caer eliminados en los penaltis ante Marruecos en el pasado Mundial, y con la ilusión de que el catalán pueda devolver a una generación de gran talento a la primera línea del fútbol europeo. Con tantos banquillos renovados y selecciones en plena reconstrucción tras el Mundial, esta edición de la Nations League se presenta como un excelente termómetro para calibrar el verdadero potencial de cada proyecto de cara a la próxima Eurocopa.

articles.title: After 28 years, Mirabai Chanu finally puts India back on Asian Games weightlifting podium
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: For 28 years, Indian weightlifting waited for this moment. There were new lifters, big names, and fresh hopes of returning to the Asian Gam.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: For 28 years, Indian weightlifting waited for this moment. There were new lifters, big names, and fresh hopes of returning to the Asian Games podium. But the medal remained out of reach.On Wednesday, Mirabai Chanu finally ended the wait.With India's hopes resting on her shoulders, the Tokyo Olympic silver medallist lifted 198kg to win silver in the women's 49kg event at the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya.It was India's first Asian Games weightlifting medal since Karnam Malleswari won silver at the 1998 Bangkok Games.The wait of 28 yearsIndia's last Asian Games weightlifting medal came in 1998, when Malleswari won silver in Bangkok. India did not win a weightlifting medal at the 2002 Asian Games in Busan. The 2006 Asian Games in Doha brought another setback. The International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) suspended the Indian Weightlifting Federation following multiple positive doping tests. India did not take part in the weightlifting events after the government failed to pay a USD 50,000 fine to the IWF to lift the suspension.At the 2010 Asian Games in Guangzhou, India sent 12 weightlifters but returned without a medal.Four years later in Incheon, India fielded seven weightlifters. The team included names such as Sathish Sivalingam, Khumukcham Sanjita Chanu, Mirabai and Punam Yadav. But once again, Indian weightlifters returned empty-handed.The 2018 Asian Games in Jakarta and Palembang also ended without an Indian weightlifting medal. India fielded four lifters, with Sathish Sivalingam among the senior names and medal contenders.Then came the 2022 Asian Games, which were held in Hangzhou in 2023.There was fresh hope as Mirabai was one of India's leading medal contenders. India sent only two female weightlifters - Mirabai and Bindyarani Devi. Both came close, but India's wait continued. Mirabai narrowly missed a medal at the Hangzhou Asian Games in 2023. She finished fourth after an injury prevented her from completing her final clean and jerk attempt.Nagoya brought another chanceWhen the Asian Games arrived in 2026, Mirabai once again carried India's hopes. She entered the competition with confidence after winning her third straight Commonwealth Games gold in Glasgow earlier this year. But the Asian Games presented a stronger challenge, with North Korea's defending champion and world champion Ri Song Gum leading the field.This time, Mirabai made the opportunity count. Mirabai finished with a total of 198kg in Nagoya. She lifted 87kg in the snatch before producing a best lift of 111kg in the clean and jerk. That was enough for silver and ended India's 28-year wait for an Asian Games weightlifting medal.Ri Song Gum won gold with a record-breaking total of 215kg. She lifted 94kg in the snatch and 121kg in the clean and jerk. Indonesia's Luluk Diana Tri Wijayana won bronze with a total of 191kg.For Mirabai, the silver was more than just another medal. She had won an Olympic silver, World Championship medals and multiple Commonwealth Games titles. But an Asian Games medal had remained missing from her collection.And after 28 years, Indian weightlifting was back among the medals.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian Games hockey: Deepika's nine-goal show powers India to 20-1 win over Thailand
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: Deepika produced a stunning nine-goal show as India continued their dominant run in women's hockey at the 2026 Asian Games, thrashing Thail.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Deepika produced a stunning nine-goal show as India continued their dominant run in women's hockey at the 2026 Asian Games, thrashing Thailand 20-1 in their Pool B match at the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium on Wednesday.The forward and drag-flick specialist converted all nine of her goals from penalty corners as India registered their third straight victory of the competition.The win kept the Sjoerd Marijne-coached side at the top of the Pool B standings.Deepika's nine-goal showDeepika was the star of the match, scoring nine times in a remarkable individual performance.All nine goals came from penalty corners, with Deepika repeatedly finding a way past the Thailand defence as India dominated the contest.Navneet Kaur added four goals, while Rutuja Pisal completed her hat-trick.Neha, Lalremsiami, Sakshi Rana and captain Salima Tete also found the net as India maintained pressure throughout the match.Thailand find a late goalThailand managed to avoid a clean sheet only late in the fourth quarter.Supansa Samanso scored Thailand's only goal with a drag-flick from a penalty corner. Her effort took a slight deflection before finding its way into the Indian goal.It was the only time Thailand managed to beat the Indian defence.India continue their goal rushIndia had opened their campaign with a 19-0 win over Uzbekistan before following it up with a 17-1 victory over Indonesia.Deepika had also scored a hat-trick against Indonesia, while Rutuja and Navneet also hit three goals each in that match.Sunelita Toppo, Lalremsiami and Sakshi scored two goals apiece, while Ishika and Salima also found the target.India took some time to settle against Indonesia, but Deepika broke the deadlock in the eighth minute after India earned four penalty corners in quick succession.Against Thailand, Deepika once again showed why she is such an important part of India's penalty-corner attack.Japan next for IndiaIndia will next face Japan on Friday as they look to strengthen their position ahead of the knockout stages.The Indian team are looking to improve on their bronze-medal finish at the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Games.They are also chasing their first Asian Games gold in women's hockey since 1982, when India won the inaugural women's hockey title at the Games on home soil.With three straight wins and 56 goals in their opening matches, India have made a strong start to their Pool B campaign.And after Deepika's nine-goal performance against Thailand, India's attacking threat looks even stronger heading into the next stage of the competition.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Indian Wushu player Roshibina Devi entered the women's 60kg Sanda final at the Asian Games on Wednesday, assuring India of at least a silver medal and matching the country's best-ever result in Wushu at the Games.Roshibina defeated Indonesia's Thania Kusumaningtyas 2-0 in the semifinal to book her place in the final.The 25-year-old was not part of India's original squad for the Games. She got into the team after Divyanshi suffered an injury, opening up a place in the squad.Roshibina had won silver at the previous Asian Games in Hangzhou. With a place in the final this time, she is guaranteed at least another silver and will now fight for gold.She will face China's Zhang Xiaoyu in the women's 60kg Sanda final on Thursday.Roshibina has now won medals in three successive editions of the Asian Games, having claimed a bronze medal and a silver medal in the previous two editions.Asian Games full coverage | Schedule | Medal tallyWho is Roshibina Devi?Born on December 30, 2000, in Kwasiphai Mayai Leikai in Manipur's Bishnupur district, Roshibina competes in the Sanda discipline of wushu, a combat sport that combines striking and throwing techniques.She first announced herself on the Asian Games stage at Jakarta 2018, where she competed in the women's 60kg Sanda category. Roshibina defeated Pakistan's Mubashra Akhtar in the quarterfinals to assure herself of a medal before losing to China's Cai Yingying in the semifinal.Five years later, at the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Games, Roshibina went one better. She reached the women's 60kg final and claimed silver after losing to China's Wu Xiaowei.Her performance at Hangzhou made her one of India's established names in wushu, and she was subsequently conferred the Arjuna Award for 2023.At Aichi-Nagoya, Roshibina has now assured herself of another podium finish. She first defeated Bangladesh's Shika Khatun in the pre-quarterfinals on Monday before producing a 5-0 victory over Chu Man Sin in the quarterfinals and now defeating Indonesia's Thania Kusumaningtyas 2-0 in the semifinal.She will face China's Zhang Xiaoyu in the women's 60kg Sanda final on Thursday at 6:10 am IST.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Incombustible Chusovitina: ¡A la final de salto de los Juegos Asiáticos con 51 años!
articles.standfirst: La gimnasta uzbeka, medallista olímpica y mundial de salto, sigue compitiendo y aspira a lograr la plaza para los Juegos Olímpicos de Los Ángeles
articles.summary: La gimnasta uzbeka, medallista olímpica y mundial de salto, sigue compitiendo y aspira a lograr la plaza para los Juegos Olímpicos de Los Ángeles
articles.body: Treinta y dos años después de su debut en los Juegos Asiáticos, la gimnasta uzbeka Oksana Chusovitina se ha clasificado para la final de salto de esta competición continental... ¡con 51 años! "Si lo que hago puede inspirar a otros, eso también me hace feliz. Hacer lo que quiero es muy importante para mí", aseguró la gimnasta incombustible, que atesora once medallas mundiales y ocho en los Juegos Asiáticos, además de dos olímpicas. Ahora Chusovitina se clasificó en cuarta posición para la final, con una puntuación de13.266, tras una calificación encabezada por la coreana Yeo Seojeong (14.466). Pero la uzbeka, que disputa sus séptimos Juegos Asiáticos, sigue soñando con estar en Los Ángeles 2028. "Intentaré clasificarme”, dijo Chusovitina a la prensa al ser preguntada sobre sus planes futuros. “Es deporte, es gimnasia. Si es posible, intentaré competir en Los Ángeles”. La gimnasta insistió en que ahora se divierte con la gimnasia, por lo que no piensa en la retirada. “Ahora siento más placer y emoción. Simplemente disfruto de la competición. Por fin, después de tantos años, empiezo a sentir emociones positivas y placer gracias a la gimnasia”

articles.title: Who is Prachiti Nagpurkar? The chartered accountant who quit lucrative career to become India's first MMA referee at Asian Games 2026
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: Maharashtra's Prachiti Nagpurkar left behind a career in chartered accountancy to follow her passion for mixed martial arts. Prachiti becam.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Maharashtra's Prachiti Nagpurkar left behind a career in chartered accountancy to follow her passion for mixed martial arts. Prachiti became the first Indian official to referee a mixed martial arts bout at the Asian Games when she took charge of one of the semifinal bouts at the Nagoya City Inae Sports Center. MMA made its debut at the continental multi-sport event in Aichi-Nagoya.For Prachiti, the achievement was about more than officiating a fight. It was about representing India in a sport she has loved for years.Who is Prachiti Nagpurkar?Prachiti started her MMA officiating journey in 2022, but her association with the sport began earlier.She has been training in MMA since 2019 and also owns an MMA gym in Mumbai. She trains students at the gym, including a team of female fighters whom she believes are the next generation of the sport.Asked about the qualifications required to become an MMA official, she said:"First thing is, you have to be training in MMA. I own an MMA gym in Mumbai. I have been doing it since 2019. I have a couple of students, one of them won medal at Asian Youth Games."I have a couple of people that I train with. I actually have a team of female fighters who are going to be the next generation."From chartered accountant to MMA refereePrachiti's journey from chartered accountancy to MMA officiating has been unconventional. Despite having a professional qualification, she chose to pursue her passion for the sport."Though I'm a chartered accountant, Mixed Martial Arts is my love, my passion. I have left CA and now I am on officiating MMA matches."It never differentiated that I was a female. In India, I also referee male fights and there are big, big men standing. I'm a small female and I've found my way about it. I do not feel intimidated anymore. I'm very, very confident with my rules and in the cage."Most MMA fights in India take place inside a fenced enclosure known as a cage or octagon.Prachiti believes her background in both academics and martial arts helped her become an official."I started my journey because I'm a chartered accountant and I'm a martial artist. I have a combination of brains and physical strength. And I thought, why not use it. Studying is a part of me. So I did a lot of exams to become a judge and a referee."You have to pass the national qualification first. There are levels C, B, A. Once you become A level, then you can go on to the Asian qualification. Then you can go to the world qualification."I started with C, then I became a B, then A. After that, I went on to the international level with the Asian Federation. I've just started, so I'm a level C with the Asian Federation right now. For this, I had to give a couple of exams, theory exams, practical exams, multiple times."'We are a part of history here'Being part of MMA's Asian Games debut made the occasion even more special for Prachiti."We are a part of history here. MMA is my sport and seeing my sport come to Asian Games and representing my country as a referee has been a very surreal experience. I always dreamt of representing my country. I'm the first Indian official to be a match referee in MMA. I'm not just the first woman official," Prachiti said.She also believes athletes are not the only ones who can represent their country at major sporting events."Even if you can't represent your country as an athlete, the journey never ends. You can always represent your country in some other capacity, be a judge, an official and your name still comes along with your country name and trust me that feeling is very special."'The queen of the cage'Prachiti has also officiated several men's bouts and says she is comfortable working in a sport traditionally dominated by men."I'm very proud to say that in a male-dominated sport, it's a female official who got the first chance to referee at such a big level. I did refereeing in nine out of ten male fights recently."I'm very confident and I love it that I'm a petite female in the cage and I can boss around as the queen of the cage. I love that feeling," said Prachiti who began her journey in 2022.She also has a message for women looking to enter sports that have traditionally been dominated by men."I want to say to all females out there, we can go out there and do our best even if it's a male-dominated sport."From Asian Games qualifiers to international eventsPrachiti's Asian Games assignment was not her only international officiating experience this year.She has officiated at the Asian Games qualifiers and the Asian Championships in Uzbekistan and China. She has also worked at the Southeast Asian Games.There were two other Indians officiating in the Asian Games MMA competition, which concluded on Monday. However, they were judges and not referees.Prachiti's appearance as a referee therefore marked a first for Indian MMA officiating at the Asian Games.Hoping MMA grows in IndiaPrachiti hopes MMA will receive a further boost after making its Asian Games debut and Suchika Tariyal winning a bronze medal.Her journey from chartered accountancy to the MMA cage has given her a place in Indian sports history and shown another way of representing the country beyond being an athlete.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'We were really looking forward to Japan': Teary-eyed Manu Bhaker remembers late coach Jaspal Rana
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NAGOYA: Manu Bhaker wore a disappointed look after finishing fifth (181.1) in the women’s 10m air pistol event. The position was unchanged from the pr.
articles.body: NAGOYA: Manu Bhaker wore a disappointed look after finishing fifth (181.1) in the women’s 10m air pistol event. The position was unchanged from the previous edition of the Asian Games, but almost everything else had.In Hangzhou, she had been part of the gold-winning trio in the team event. More importantly, she had reunited with her coach Jaspal Rana in the run-up to the Games.This time, she had neither the medal nor the man who had been such a significant part of her shooting journey.As Manu walked into the mixed zone after the final, it was evident she was struggling to hold back her emotions. She managed to do so until the conversation turned to Rana, who passed away in June.Rana, one of the most decorated shooters in Asian Games history with eight medals, including four gold across three editions, had missed the Hangzhou Games as he was not part of the Indian contingent.Manu and Rana had been looking forward to this Games. It was not to be.“We were really looking forward to Japan,” said the 24-year-old, before tears began rolling down her cheeks.She stepped away for a few minutes to compose herself before returning.“I remember what he said, not once or twice, but all the time. It just stays with you. When a person has been a big part of your life, it just stays. It’s very natural,” she said.“Of all the things he said, what I remember the most is about the process. He was just so adamant about the process — that at any given point in your life, you have to be able to give your best performance and follow your process.”Then came a thought that seemed to go beyond shooting.“Life is just very unpredictable. So, live your life to the fullest, be kind to everyone,” she said.The past few months have been particularly difficult for Manu. Along with losing Rana, she also lost her grandmother.There had been a popular expectation of a medal in Nagoya, and Manu felt the weight of that expectation. “I genuinely tried my best. I am really sorry that I was not able to make it to the podium. I hope that I will be able to do better,” she said.The final itself mirrored the turmoil of the preceding months.Manu made a steady start and was third after the opening set, only for an 8.9 to send her tumbling to seventh. She fought back with a 10.1 and a 10.4, before an 10.8 lifted her from the brink of elimination. The rollercoaster continued. Another 10.8 took her back to third, but a 9.6 in the next series ended her medal hopes and left her fifth.Her coach Jelena Arunovic was not surprised by the performance. “During our training in Bhopal, finals-like practice sessions were organised. Compare the performance from there to here, it’s slightly better. This is what my coach told me as well,” said Manu.As she walked away, the panda pimple patch on her left cheek was perhaps the only thing that looked cheerful.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Dave Allen reveals blockbuster fight talks against Anthony Joshua’s opponent that could happen early next year
articles.summary: International Sports News: Dave Allen is closing in on a potential showdown with former unified heavyweight world champion Andy Ruiz Jr. The British heavyweight has revealed tha.
articles.body: Dave Allen is closing in on a potential showdown with former unified heavyweight world champion Andy Ruiz Jr. The British heavyweight has revealed that the fight could take place in Sheffield early next year, with Allen welcoming the opportunity.The 34-year-old’s recent fight with Thomas Carty ended in bizarre fashion after the Irishman fell through the ropes and was unable to continue. Now, Allen could face one of the biggest names of his career, despite openly admitting the challenge posed by Ruiz.Dave Allen ready for Andy Ruiz Jr heavyweight showdownDave Allen has already made it clear that he is interested in facing Andy Ruiz Jr if the proposed fight becomes official.Speaking on SunSport’s Corner Talk, Allen revealed, “It could happen early next year in Sheffield and I am all for it, what have I got to lose? Andy Ruiz just lost so he needs a comeback fight and I probably only have one big fight left. I am happy for the fight. If I get paid a fortune to fight the guy who once upon a time was THE guy, of course I am going to do it.”Ruiz became a major name in boxing in 2019 when he shocked Anthony Joshua in New York. The Mexican dropped Joshua four times before stopping him and becoming the first Mexican heavyweight world champion.However, Ruiz lost the rematch later that year. He has also struggled for consistency in recent years.Ruiz most recently suffered a defeat to Damian Knyba, adding another setback to his record. A comeback fight could now see him share the ring with Allen.Allen, meanwhile, has built a reputation as a popular heavyweight and a ticket-selling attraction.His professional record stands at 27 wins, nine defeats and two draws. His career has also included tough fights against Dillian Whyte, Luis Ortiz, Tony Yoka and David Price.Allen has previously spoken openly about his gambling addiction and the difficult period it caused in his life. He later turned his life around and has since focused on his family and other sources of income.Despite his record, Allen remains a popular figure with boxing fans. He also has more than 100,000 followers on TikTok.The British fighter believes that popularity gives him the chance to compete in big events.“People say I don’t deserve these fights but if people want to come and pay and watch me try to entertain them and win the fight then that’s up to them. I don’t need to box anymore, financially, which is nice. I am not the same guy anymore, I used to be a tough guy. That’s why I admire the likes of Anthony Joshua, I am definitely not as rich as him and I definitely wouldn’t fight if I was”, he said.Allen is also realistic about the huge gap in experience and ability between himself and Ruiz.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Celtics Starter Left Off ESPN Top 100 After Breakout Season
articles.summary: Neemias Queta of the Boston Celtics fell just short of ESPN’s top 100 rankings for the 2026-27 season, but he did earn a spot on the network’s list of player...
articles.body:
Neemias Queta of the Boston Celtics fell just short of ESPN's top 100 rankings for the 2026-27 season, but he did earn a spot on the network's list of players to watch heading into next year.

The Celtics center, 27, put together a career-best campaign last season. He averaged 10.4 points, 8.4 rebounds and 1.3 blocks across 76 starts. His playing time nearly doubled from the previous year. It jumped to 25.3 minutes per game after Boston moved on from Kristaps Porzingis via trade. The Celtics also lost Al Horford to the Golden State Warriors in free agency. That cleared a path for Queta to take over the starting job.

ESPN's Zach Kram highlighted just how significant that jump was. Queta had never crossed 1,000 minutes in a season before. He logged 1,926 last year once he was thrust into the starting role. Boston's net rating improved by 8.6 points with Queta on the floor compared to off it. His defensive impact stood out in particular. Opponents shot just 51 percent at the rim when Queta was the nearest defender. That mark ranked seventh among 71 players who defended at least 200 such attempts.

Queta's strong regular season came with some rough patches in the playoffs, and his relatively limited track record as a full-time starter kept him off the actual top-100 list. Kram pointed to his struggles against Joel Embiid in the postseason as part of the counterargument, while also noting real optimism going forward. He suggested Queta and new Celtics addition Mitchell Robinson could form one of the more disruptive big-man duos in the league this season.

ESPN released the 100-51 portion of its rankings Tuesday. Paul George landed at No. 67. Payton Pritchard came in at No. 70. The top 50 will be published separately at a later date. Derrick White has cracked that upper tier in each of the past two seasons. He checked in at No. 26 last year after jumping 13 spots from No. 39 the year before. articles.title: Aberdeen's attacking issues laid bare
articles.summary: The 48 chances created by Stephen Robinson's side is the lowest tally in the division - same for their 37 chances from open play - while they have the fewest...
articles.body:
The stats behind the Dons' start to the Premiership season flag up some attacking concerns.

The 48 chances created by Stephen Robinson's side is the lowest tally in the division - same for their 37 chances from open play - while they have the fewest shots on target (18) and second-fewest shots (70).

It must be noted Aberdeen haven't had the kindest fixtures, with Robinson keen to point out they have faced five of last season's top-six teams in their opening seven games.

Eight points have been accrued, leaving the Dons seventh in a congested table and just two points shy of fourth, so there's no reason for panic.

Still, the Pittodrie side have netted just seven league goals - only bottom two Falkirk and Kilmarnock have scored fewer - and their xG (expected goals) is a league-low 7.16, suggesting opportunities have not exactly been flowing.

That is backed up by what Opta terms 'big chances' - the Dons' tally of nine is above only Falkirk, and their 137 touches in the opposition box is the third fewest.

Robinson's Aberdeen are not a ball-dominant team - their average possession 45.09% ranks 10th in the top flight - but they do possess a prowess at set-pieces. They have scored three goals and created 11 chances - the third-highest in the league - from dead balls.

And if the Dons could become more productive, they have a striker capable of profiting. Kevin Nisbet has netted 43% of the team's league goals - three of seven - from just four shots on target and also weighed in with two assists.

Dons fans, what do you make of the attacking threat in Robinson's side? Share your views here.

articles.title: Edgewood's Heinbaugh advances to D-II district individually in boys golf
articles.summary: Ashtabula County boys golf teams were shut out of the Division II district tournament Tuesday. But it wasn't a total loss, as one individual advanced to the...
articles.body:
Ashtabula County boys golf teams were shut out of the Division II district tournament Tuesday.

But it wasn't a total loss, as one individual advanced to the next round.

Edgewood's Jackson Heinbaugh qualified to the district as an individual with an 41-40-81 at the Quail Hollow Sectional Tuesday.

The sophomore tied Hawken senior Owen Khan and Kirtland senior Nick Nead, but earned the district spot with a birdie on the first playoff hole.

"Going into the playoff, I knew it wasn't going to be easy going up against two upperclassmen," Heinbaugh said. "I had known that those boys would have a big distance advantage on me, but I knew that with accuracy, I could for sure make up for it."

Heinbaugh said he focused on playing his own round.

"I'm grateful for the opportunity to play [Tuesday], and happy that I qualified," he said.

Warriors coach Ben Frable said Heinbaugh played a steady round.

"He didn't get too high on good holes, then didn't get down on himself after bad holes," Frable said. "He has been playing some really good golf these last couple of weeks. For him to win that playoff against two other seasoned golfers says a lot about his mental game. That was a great time to have his first birdie of the day."

Akron Springfield sophomore Nathan Vorthong, with a 43-34-77 and Kirtland junior John Scalish, 41-39-80, were the other two individual qualifiers.

The top three teams and three individuals not on a qualifying team qualified for the district tournament, which is scheduled for next Tuesday at Windmill Lakes.

articles.title: Viel Scores Twice as Lightning Fall to Predators 3-2
articles.summary: The Lightning’s 3-2 preseason loss to the Nashville Predators on Tuesday night wasn’t the result Tampa Bay wanted, but it did provide a look at a new line co...
articles.body:
The Lightning 's 3-2 preseason loss to the Nashville Predators on Tuesday night wasn't the result Tampa Bay wanted, but it did provide a look at a new line combination.

Tampa Bay carried a two-goal lead into the final seven minutes of regulation, thanks to a pair of goals from newly signed forward Jeffrey Viel .

With Yanni Gourde expected to miss time after undergoing hip surgery, Viel skated on a line with Zemgus Girgensons and Pontus Holmberg . The trio showed early signs of chemistry in their first game together.

Girgensons helped create Tampa Bay's opening goal after getting his stick on a Nashville pass, keeping the puck in the Predators' zone. The puck went directly to Viel, who found himself with an open scoring chance and capitalized, giving the Lightning the lead.

Viel added his second goal of the night later in the game, following up his own initial attempt that was blocked to put Tampa Bay up 2-0.

The Lightning, however, couldn't hold onto the lead.

Nashville center Matthew Wood scored twice in a span of 4:11 late in the third period to tie the game and force overtime.

Then, a turnover in Tampa Bay's defensive zone led to Felix Nilsson 's game-winning goal in overtime.

"A lot of good things but we let that one get away at the end," Viel said after the game. "It's preseason and that's the time to learn so we are going to go back to work tomorrow and learn from it"

For Viel, the game provided an encouraging first look at what he can bring to Tampa Bay's lineup. The 29-year-old signed a five-year, $12.5 million contract with the Lightning this summer and is expected to bring a physical presence and some added depth to the bottom six.

The Lightning will have two more opportunities to fine-tune their lineup before the regular season begins. They'll host the Florida Panthers on Thursday before traveling to Sunrise for the preseason finale Saturday.

articles.title: Tyler Herro wore enormous shorts to recreate iconic T.J. Ford photoshoot
articles.summary: A classic image gets a second life with new Milwaukee Bucks guard.
articles.body:
Tyler Herro is now a member of the Milwaukee Bucks thanks to his inclusion in the Giannis Antetokounmpo deal. Once believed to be a foundational piece for the Miami Heat , Herro will get another opportunity to grow his star on the shores of Lake Michigan. Going from South Beach to Wisconsin is a quite a change but basketball fanbases are universal in that they will love you if you pour in buckets night after night. Herro, despite having his progression to a superstar slow considerably over the past few seasons, is capable of going off every single time he steps on the court.

It appears he also knows how to play the PR game, as evidenced by a savvy photoshoot that taps into some nostalgia.

Herro and former Bucks guard T.J. Ford recreated the latter's iconic rookie photoshoot that is still ubiquitous on the internet today.

Enormous shorts and all. The photos are tremendous—and so too is the buy-in from both involved parties.

This right here is such a smart move from Herro. If you can't have fun as an NBA player in late-September before there's any pressure, then when can you? These photoshoots are simply not that serious and it's clever to find a way to make them truly worthwhile.

Plus, for old heads like me, seeing Herro in the shorts we used to wear—which would greatly hinder the ability to ball-handle—sparks tremendous joy. I didn't really have any opinion about Herro before today and now it feels like he is one of us. Or at the very least, Elder Millennial coded. Nostalgia is really undefeated.

Then there's the thought Herro could be a trend-setter. It's not likely but it is possible that other NBA players are going to see how good he looks in the baggy fit and follow suit. Teams can start selling big ol' shorts for divorced dads to wear to the park or when taking the dog for a walk. There has to be money in this somewhere.

Fashion is cyclical and it's only a matter of time until the huge shorts look comes back in full force. It's better to be easy than it is to be late on any trend.

articles.title: Vanderbilt's defense will present Auburn with a 'unique' challenge
articles.summary: Auburn offensive coordinator Joel Gordon looks to turn the page to Vanderbilt's "unique" defensive challenges.
articles.body:
The Auburn Tigers posted 373 yards last Saturday in their loss to the Florida Gators , but it was not enough for the Tigers to pull off the win.

The Tigers got off to a slow start, ending the 1st quarter down by 3 yards and ultimately producing just 102 rushing yards. Auburn also did not have as much time with the ball as their counterparts, having just 20:44 of possession compared to Florida's 39:16.

This week, the Tigers will move on and try to bounce back against the Vanderbilt Commodores , a team without as much buzz as in previous years, but still a quality team with a 3-0 record. Auburn offensive coordinator Joel Gordon explained this week that Vanderbilt's defense presents a different challenge than Florida did last week.

"The way that they attack is a little bit different. One way or another, they force you to deal with some different schemes than what we saw last week," Gordon said. "One week at a time, you're trying to understand the presentations of challenges you face from a defense. Baylor was what Baylor was, Southern Miss, and then Florida. You're trying to understand what those things were as an offensive unit and the coaching staff, obviously, and figure out how we do well against it and what we need to fix."

Despite not posting as many yards as Florida last week, Auburn still did several things well. Byrum Brown passed for 271 yards, and the offense produced 10 plays that gained 15 or more yards; six of those were for gains of 20 or more. Gordon will look to shut down the negatives from last week's performance and capitalize on the positive moments from the Florida loss.

"I think we take the situations that we did well against Florida and move on with it, and the things we didn't do well we address and get ready, because if you don't get things fixed, people aren't going to go away," Gordon said. "They're just going to keep trying to expose the issues that you have. We have to build on the things we did, because we did a lot of good things, and we have to fix the mistakes. Vanderbilt is good on defense, but uniquely different than what the last challenge was."

Auburn battles Vanderbilt on Saturday at 3:15 p.m. CT. The Tigers hold an advantage in points per game and total yards over Vanderbilt, but the Commodores' defense ranks in the top 10 in the SEC, and the Tigers must find a way to expose Vanderbilt early to get out with a win.

articles.title: Ravens vs. Cowboys: Three early matchups to watch in Brazil
articles.summary: Simply put, the citizens of Rio de Janeiro are in for a treat at Maracanã Stadium for Ravens vs. Cowboys.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys enter Week 3 searching for momentum after very different Week 2 experiences. Dallas bounced back with a win over rival Washington, while Baltimore is trying to move past a frustrating home loss to the New Orleans Saints .

The international stage only adds to the intrigue. Before either team arrives in Brazil, several fascinating matchups are already taking shape.

Baltimore's offense has shown flashes through two weeks, but consistency remains elusive. The Ravens moved the football effectively against the Saints before managing only three second-half points. Meanwhile, Dallas enters Week 3 allowing 24 points per game and 391.5 yards per contest. The latter ranks near the bottom of the league defensively.

The Cowboys have also struggled to get off the field on third down through two games. That creates an opportunity for Lamar Jackson , Derrick Henry , Mark Andrews , and Rashod Bateman to reestablish Baltimore's offensive identity. This is especially intriguing because it also pits two first-time coordinators still trying to establish themselves.

Coordinator battles don't usually make front-page headlines, but this one deserves attention. Declan Doyle's offense looked explosive in Week 1 and productive for stretches in Week 2 before stalling late against the Saints . Christian Parker's defense, meanwhile, is still searching for consistency after Dallas underwent major defensive changes during the offseason.

Several opponents have moved the ball effectively against the Cowboys, particularly on third down. Both coaches are early in their respective tenures, and both are still shaping their units' identities. Whichever coordinator makes the better in-game adjustments could determine the outcome.

Cowboys receivers vs. Ravens cornerbacks

Few position battles on the field carry more star power. Dallas features one of the NFL's most talented receiver groups, with CeeDee Lamb leading the way and the George Pickens-Ryan Flournoy combo providing other explosive targets. Dak Prescott showed how dangerous that group can be during a four-touchdown performance against Washington.

Baltimore counters with Nate Wiggins and Marlon Humphrey , but another name bears watching. On Monday, Jesse Minter said the Ravens need to find ways to get Chidobe Awuzie on the field more after the veteran cornerback played only one defensive snap against New Orleans . Whether that results in a larger role this week remains to be seen, but Dallas presents a compelling argument for deploying additional cornerback help.

Technically, they will never share the field at the same time. Practically, this is still one of the most fascinating quarterback matchups of Week 3. Jackson remains one of the league's most dynamic players and can take over a game with either his arm or his legs. Prescott enters the matchup fresh off a four-touchdown performance that helped Dallas rebound from an opening-week loss.

Both quarterbacks will be asked to carry significant responsibility. Jackson is attempting to push Baltimore back into the win column. Prescott is trying to prove Dallas can build momentum after an uneven start. In a game featuring international travel, playoff aspirations, and two talented rosters, it wouldn't be surprising if the quarterback who makes the fewest mistakes ultimately leaves Brazil with a victory.

articles.title: Giants-Titans storylines: Moving on without Jaxson Dart
articles.summary: All of the optimism surrounding the 2026 Giants is gone. What will take its place?
articles.body:
Jaxson Dart is likely not going to be under center for any of them, but the New York Giants still have 15 games to play in the 2026 NFL season. How will they do without their young quarterback, who played like a star in an impressive Week 1 victory over the Dallas Cowboys ?

We begin to find out Sunday at MetLife Stadium when the Tennessee Dabolls — er, Titans — come to East Rutherford, N.J. for a 1 p.m. matchup. Below are some of the storylines for the week.

The latest reporting from NFL Network insider Mike Garafolo is that " there are a few timelines on the table , none of them very good, one of them season-ending" for the Giants quarterback.

While we await word on that, it is obvious Dart will not play Sunday against Tennessee. And the Giants will be without him for the foreseeable future.

How will the Giants fare without Dart, especially if he is out all season? It is possible that John Harbaugh and his veteran coaching staff squeeze every ounce of juice from this imperfect Giants' roster and they finish in the neighborhood of .500. It is also possible that a four- or five-win season, the kind of disastrous year the Giants figured was off the table due to Harbaugh's presence, is back on the table.

Beginning with the 0-2 Titans, the Giants have a three-game stretch of games that should be winnable.

Tennessee is a young, winless team coming to MetLife Stadium. They did, though, put a Week 2 scare into the Philadelphia Eagles. The 1-1 Arizona Cardinals come to MetLife in Week 4. They are expected to be one of the league's weaker teams. The Giants visit the 0-2 Washington Commanders in Week 5. The Commanders could be without star quarterback Jayden Daniels , who suffered his second dislocated left elbow in as many seasons on Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys.

If the Giants cannot win at least two of those three games, another long, miserable, losing season could follow.

Harbaugh, one of the winningest head coaches of all time, is going to be challenged over the next 15 games.

The veteran head coach promised on Tuesday that the Giants will "be fighting every step of the way."

"We haven't even come close – not even close — to playing as well as we're capable of playing as a football team," Harbaugh said. "So, that's really going to be the focus. I mean, it's going to be something we're going to have to, you deal with all the different challenges that you face and all the different adversity that you face, for sure. And even the prosperity, you learned that last week, you faced some of the prosperity, and prosperity sometimes can be more dangerous than adversity.

"All these challenges to put your best effort out there, play your best football, so you can win a football game. And we're going to do that. These guys are going to do that. That's what you get excited about. The prospect of our team playing the best football that they can play. And that's what we're working on, working as hard as we can, working like crazy as a football team to do that all together."

The Giants referred to Dart's injury as an in-game "gut punch." Harbaugh does not expect that to cause a long-term letdown.

"The guys want to go win. They want to go play," Harbaugh said. "Guys play. They'll play. They play for each other. They play for themselves. They play for their families. They play because they believe they can win the game. And it's never one person, never one person that wins or loses a football game. It's everybody. And the more good players you can have out there, the better chance you're going to have. There's no doubt about it. But you still have to be a complete team to win games.

"If you get punched in the gut, are you going down? Are you going down? Are you going to crumple to the ground, as Jack Harbaugh would say, like a sack of sour apples and just fall to the ground and just rot away and wither away into the dust. Is that what you're going to do?"

To win games, the Giants are going to have to accomplish several things:

They will have to get better play from quarterback Jameis Winston than the miserable 11 of 27 for 11 yards and an interception performance he gave them Monday night.

They will have to find some way to get explosive plays from their offense. The longest non-Dart run they have in two games is a 13-yard carry by Cam Skattebo . They have one pass completion of more than 20 yards, a 33-yard grab by Darnell Mooney .

The pass rush will have to remember that the regular season has started.

They will need to find a way to cover some of the league's best receivers.

They need to hope that injuries to stars Brian Burns , Andrew Thomas , and Malik Nabers aren't severe. Oh, and that other injuries don't continue to pile up.

We begin to find out how life after Dart will go Sunday against Tennessee.

Dart suffered the worst and most significant injury on Monday night. Still, the game against the Rams saw several other significant injuries to Giants stars.

Edge defender Brian Burns, who had a career-high 16.5 sacks last season, suffered a sprained left ankle.

Left tackle Andrew Thomas apparently suffered a groin injury on the Giants' final offensive possession.

Wide receiver Malik Nabers left the game briefly with a shoulder injury. He had just one catch for 1 yard in the game.

Cornerback Deonte Banks missed Monday's game with a calf injury. His status for Week 3 is unclear.

The initial injury report of the week comes out Wednesday afternoon. We find out more about the severity of these injuries then. With a short week before playing the Titans, it is fair to wonder just how short-handed the Giants are going to be in a game that not long ago looked like one the Giants should win.

This game has been circled on the calendar for a while simply because of the volume of former Giants — especially key Giants — who are now part of the Titans' organization.

Daboll, fired last season as Giants head coach, is now running the Tennessee offense. Daboll, of course, was instrumental in the Giants' decision to trade up last season to draft Dart.

Robinson is second on the Titans with six receptions for 47 yards, just 7.8 yards per catch. He had the only 1,000-yard season of his career with the Giants last season.

Bellinger has just one catch in two games, one of which he started.

Schlottmann has started both Tennessee games at center. Through two games, Schlottmann's Pro Football and Sports Network 'Impact Score' is 72.6. For the Giants, starting center John Michael Schmitz is at 73.6. Both scores are slightly below what PFSN considers league average, a score of 75.0.

The Giants' defense was supposed to be built around what they hoped would be a dominant pass rush.

Burns is coming off a career-best season. Abdul Carter was drafted No. 3 overall in hopes he would be a game-wrecking pass rusher. He looked in the summer like he was about to fulfill that promise. Kayvon Thibodeaux has at times been a good, but not great, pass rusher. No. 5 overall pick Arvell Reese is an inside linebacker with pass rush potential. Interior defensive linemen Chauncey Golston and Darius Alexander have pass rush ability. Defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson's defense used creative schemes to pressure Giants' quarterbacks throughout training camp.

Through two weeks of the regular season, none of that talent, potential, and summer promise has mattered. The pass rush has been non-existent.

The Giants have one quarterback sack. Per NextGenStats, their 1.4% sack rate is 31st in the league. Only the woeful Miami Dolphins , who do not have a sack yet, are worse.

The Giants' pressure rate of 26.1, again per NGS, is the worst in the league. The ball is coming out quickly against New York, with the 2.69-second time to throw against the Giants 26th overall. That is .41 seconds faster than league average. Still, the pressure rate isn't good enough.

Against the Rams, the Giants' pressure rate was even worse:

The "Get-Off" time for Giants defensive linemen — the time is takes for them to cross the line of scrimmage — is worst in the league at .94 seconds. If the ball is coming out quickly, and your linemen are getting off the ball slowly, that is a bad combination.

The Giants are giving up +.41 Expected Points Added (EPA) per pass play. Only the Dolphins are worse.

We knew entering the season that the Giants' pass rush was going to have to cover for a questionable secondary. So far, it has not not.

articles.title: Kylie Kelce Celebrates Young Female Athletes’ ‘Confidence’ by Awarding One Girls’ Sports Team a Trip to the World Cup
articles.summary: Kylie Kelce teams up with Dove for “Back Her Game,” a nationwide search to find a girls’ team that embodies the joy of sports — and help them win big
articles.body:
Kylie Kelce partnered with Dove to launch a contest promoting body confidence and participation in girls' sports teams

The winning team will receive a trip to a major sporting event and new team kits

The initiative aims to help girls feel confident and stay in the game

Kylie Kelce is your biggest cheerleader.

As a mom to four girls and former competitive field hockey player herself, Kelce teamed up with Dove for a special contest designed in an effort to champion women's sports and encourage "girls everywhere" to stay in the game.

The contest, called "Back Her Game," is a nationwide search to find one girls' sports team that embodies joy and confidence while playing the sport they love. The winning team's prize? A trip to Brazil to experience the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup.

"Sports can give girls so much — friendship, confidence, teamwork and memories that stay with them for life — but that only happens when they feel supported enough to keep playing," Kelce, 34, said in a statement, per the Dove press release.

"As a coach, I love that this campaign shines a light on girls' sports teams that show up for each other to remind girls everywhere that they belong on the field exactly as they are," continued Kelce, a Dove partner and wife Philadelphia Eagles star Jason Kelce.

The contest was inspired by the broader Dove commitment to help keep girls confident and in the game after research done by the brand showed that one in two girls who quit sports have been the subject of body criticism.

Kelce herself has spoken to PEOPLE in the past about how success in her sport enabled her to overcome any self-doubt about her own body, and instead focus on all the positive attributes she possessed.

"Early on, I was able to drown out these ideas of, 'I'm too tall,' or, 'My legs are too thick,' because, in my head, I was like, 'I'm tall and I have reach,' and, 'My legs are thick because they're strong,' " she told PEOPLE of her field hockey career . "I was able to see that narrative very early on because of the way my body applied to field hockey, and that made it so much easier to understand that your body isn't about how it looks — your body is about how strong you can be, how does it work for you and what can it do instead."

To help other girls develop that same feeling of empowerment, Dove developed its Body Confident Sport program through its Self-Esteem Project, which is designed to supply coaches with the tools to build body confidence among girls ages 11 to 17 and help create more supportive sports settings.

Through Back Her Game, Dove is searching for teams that are fostering supportive environments where female athletes can strengthen confidence, feel like they belong and have fun while playing sports.

Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE's free sports newsletter — sign up now!

Soccer legends including Mia Hamm and Alyssa Thompson are also helping spread the word about the search to grant the winning team the trip of a lifetime, in addition to new team uniforms and a Body Confident Sport session to help the coach empower his or her team to recognize everything their bodies are capable of.

The contest kicks off on Wednesday, Sept. 23 and runs through Sunday, Oct. 4. To enter, eligible coaches of girls' teams with players between the ages of 13 and 18 can post a public in-feed video to Instagram or TikTok showcasing how their team brings confidence to the field, tagging @dove and using #KeepHerConfident and #Contest in the caption.

Dove will choose the winning team whose coach's submission most authentically displays the joy and confidence they bring to their sport.

As Kelce knows, focusing on the joy and confidence is key to success, whether that's on the field or raising her own daughters.

"If you make sure that you build the girls up, whether it's at practice, whether it's at home, you can build these girls up with confidence so that when someone, some silly person, somewhere along their way, decides to try and switch up the messaging, they've had so much joy just compounded into their ears that it drowns it out and it's a non-issue," she explained to PEOPLE in January while discussing her Super Bowl partnership with Dove. "Because they're like, 'That's so silly that you said that. But I actually heard so many other times how amazing my body is, so it doesn't matter that you said that.'"

articles.title: Seahawks reportedly thought Mike Macdonald’s Sean Payton story was off-the-record
articles.summary: Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald is making headlines for a story he told reporter Graham Bensinger in a recent interview, only the story was never...
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald is making headlines for a story he told reporter Graham Bensinger in a recent interview, only the story was never intended for public consumption.

In a now-viral video clip from Bensinger's interview with Macdonald, the Seahawks coach explains that, prior to the team's Week 1 game against the Denver Broncos in 2024, the team compiled fan-shot video clips from Broncos training camp to study what plays they might run in the opener. When Broncos head coach Sean Payton caught wind of the effort midseason, Macdonald says Payton called Seahawks general manager John Scheider completely incensed and threatened to come out publicly with Connor Stallions-esque accusations. In response, the Seahawks countered by saying they'd sue if Payton and the Broncos went public, because the suggestion that Seattle was planting people at Broncos training camp to videotape practice was untrue.

The story itself is fascinating, and both Macdonald and Payton are sure to get some questions about it during upcoming press conferences. But perhaps equally fascinating is the circumstances surrounding the clip. The conversation between Macdonald and Bensinger occurred while the two were mic'd up, but seemingly before the interview formally began. The video clip shows a wide shot of the set with camera, audio, and lighting gear all in frame. The primary cameras, it would seem, were not yet rolling.

And according to Mike Florio in Pro Football Talk , the Seahawks had no idea that part of the conversation was even recorded until the video began to circulate on social media Tuesday morning. Additionally, the team is characterizing that portion of the conversation as "more off than on" the record, suggesting that Bensinger should've used some discretion before releasing it.

Of course, that decision is purely up to the journalist. If there was no prior arrangement that part of the conversation would be off-the-record, Bensinger is under no obligation to keep what Macdonald said under wraps.

It is unusual, however, for Bensinger to release this clip in the first place. While very interesting and even quite newsworthy, publicizing this part of the conversation was a surefire way to upset the Seahawks and likely Macdonald himself. It could also have the unintended consequence of making future interview subjects weary of agreeing to sit down with Bensinger in the first place.

While not often spoken about, this is the type of calculation reporters will make many times throughout their careers. If they deem a story is big enough to warrant burning a bridge or two, they'll publish it. If they deem it's better to keep the information private or squirrel it away for later in order to maintain a relationship with a source, they won't.

It appears Bensinger made the calculation that this story was worth getting in front of people, even if the Seahawks will be upset about it.

articles.title: Cam Heyward calls out Steelers O-line miscommunication
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers captain Cameron Heyward highlighted O-line miscommunication as a critical issue after Aaron Rodgers faced heavy pressure.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers ' Week 2 loss to the New England Patriots exposed a glaring vulnerability that threatens to derail their entire season - offensive line protection, or the severe lack thereof. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers was under constant siege, facing pressure on a staggering 47% of his drop-backs. For a 42-year-old caller operating behind a newly installed offense, that level of exposure is a recipe for disaster.

While public frustration has largely targeted skill-player execution and play-calling, the tape reveals that systemic miscommunications upfront are the root cause of the dysfunction. Unblocked pass rushers repeatedly forced Rodgers off his spots and into punishing hits.

On a recent episode of Cameron Heyward 's podcast, " Not Just Football with Cam Heyward ," his co-host Hayden Walsh captured the collective anxiety of the fan base, noting, "I think Aaron was pressured on 47% of his drop backs on Sunday. Cam, that is a ridiculous number. That is terrifying. Especially because Aaron, listen, I don't want to make too much of the age, but he can't take hits like he took Sunday."

Heyward didn't hide from the offensive line's struggles, identifying breakdowns in basic pre-snap communication as the main culprit behind free runners coming through the front.

"Communication, when someone comes free, that is because of communication," Heyward explained. "Cohesion, that also plays a big part. You got to be able to know what to expect with your group."

Without clean pockets, Mike McCarthy's play-action scheme remains entirely neutralized, placing immense strain on Rodgers to make off-platform hero plays.

Heyward emphasized that building chemistry and fixing assignment errors are non-negotiable if the unit expects to turn things around before facing fierce divisional pass rushes. As Pittsburgh prepares for a crucial AFC North showdown with Cincinnati , rectifying these protection lapses isn't just about unlocking the passing game; it's about keeping their franchise quarterback healthy for the long haul.

articles.title: Denny Hamlin: Carson Hocevar Always Picks the ‘Nuclear Option’
articles.summary: With Ryan Blaney sitting across from him, Denny Hamlin broke down the Bristol wreck and said Carson Hocevar always reaches for the nuclear option. Hamlin als...
articles.body:
Denny Hamlin says Carson Hocevar had two choices at Bristol, and he took the one that always ends with someone in the wall. Hamlin made the case with Ryan Blaney sitting across the table from him on the Actions Detrimental podcast this week.

The wreck and the fight have driven motorsports talk since Saturday night. Blaney called it a 50/50 deal with no clear villain. Hamlin agreed the move sat in that gray area, but he said Hocevar reaches for the same tool every time.

"My thoughts on it was that I thought Carson had two options. One was the nuclear option, which is the, 'Okay, if you're going to come down when I've got my run, I'm not lifting.' That's one option."

"That's the nuclear option, which is you know the outcome. That guy is going to wreck. The other option, in my opinion, is that you check up slightly, and then when you get into the corner, he probably should shuck you then."

Hamlin said the second option usually ends the argument on the track instead of on pit road.

"One is to just plow through them, and whatever happens to them happens to them. The other is, 'Okay, I'm going to lift, but then I'm going to give you the business once we get into the corner.' And that typically will lead into something that doesn't escalate a whole lot further."

"So my thing was that he always chooses the nuclear option, which is, 'Well, I'm there, so I'm not lifting.' And so that's the racing part of it that definitely is tough, but everyone has a way of doing it."

Hamlin was careful to say he is not going after Hocevar. He pointed out that Hocevar spun him at Sonoma and that he gave him the benefit of the doubt then.

Hamlin Says He Learned the Same Lesson in 2017

Hamlin's take comes from experience on the other side of it. With three laps left in the fall 2017 race at Martinsville Speedway , Chase Elliott tried to block Hamlin for the lead and Hamlin spun him. The caution sent the race to overtime and handed the win to Hamlin's teammate, Kyle Busch .

"We all make decisions, right? And you see up there, it was one with Chase Elliott at Martinsville and one where I was, like, thinking, 'Okay, I'm just going to get him off the bottom here.' Well, you can't expect a guy to control his car when you've got his rear tires lifted up on the entry, right?"

"So there's certain mistakes that we make through our careers that certainly we learn from. And, yeah, that sucks that you ended up wrecked in that situation."

Hamlin said every driver has a code and that rivals learn to read it. His argument is that Hocevar's code leaves no middle setting.

The wreck cost Blaney more than a finish. He led a race-high 202 laps at Bristol, then went to the garage in 33rd and dropped to sixth in the standings, 52 points behind leader Kyle Larson . Hocevar finished third and sits eighth.

The NASCAR Cup Series returns Sunday with the Hollywood Casino 400 at Kansas Speedway , where both drivers will be back on track, with coverage at 3 p.m. ET on USA Network.
