articles.title: 1 Bold Prediction for Every NHL Team for the 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: Can you believe we are less than one week away from dropping the puck on the 2026-27 NHL season?
articles.body:
Can you believe we are less than one week away from dropping the puck on the 2026-27 NHL season?

A new year of drama, triumphs, and disappointments awaits as teams warm up in the preseason and finalize their rosters.

Just how far can Macklin Celebrini and the Sharks go? Are the Leafs back in the playoff conversation with Gavin McKenna in the fold? Is Connor Hellebuyck spending the year ice fishing?

Here is one bold prediction for every NHL team for the 2026-27 season.

ANA | BOS | BUF | CAR | CBJ | CGY | CHI | COL | DAL | DET | EDM | FLA | LAK | MIN | MTL | NJD | NSH | NYI | NYR | OTT | PHI | PIT | SEA | SJS | STL | TBL | TOR | UTA | VAN | VGK | WPG | WSH

Yes, the Leo Carlsson offer sheet put the Ducks in a tough spot, but at the end of the day, they got him signed. They also managed to come to an agreement with top goal-scorer Cutter Gauthier.

Are these youngsters overpaid? Maybe. Are they signed and as focused as can be headed into the season? Absolutely.

Through no fault of David Pastrňák, Charlie McAvoy, and/or Jeremy Swayman, it's hard to see the Bruins improving on, or even repeating, last year's first-round exit.

Pavel Zacha and Morgan Geekie both had career seasons last year, and it really concealed the depth issues throughout this roster.

JJ Peterka is a wonderful addition, Marco Sturm has been great as head coach, and yet, this roster just feels like pieces of something great that may or may not happen one day, but not today.

Buffalo Sabres: We're Under-Reacting About Off-Season Departures

The Sabres' young core took real steps last season, and the cathartic two-round playoff run is just the beginning of an era of optimism for Buffalo.

Still, the losses of Alex Tuch and Bowen Byram make this roster objectively worse and I'm not sure we're talking about it enough.

Knowing GM Jarmo Kekäläinen, though, the front office could be playing the long game. There's a good enough chance that the Sabres are seeing what they've got in the first half of the season with the intent of addressing deficits at the deadline.

Calgary Flames: Šimon Nemec Will Struggle At First

We're at the turning point in the Flames' rebuild, where the prospect pool is overflowing, yet the team on the ice just isn't close to being "there" yet. It's always interesting when the first NHL-ready pieces start rolling in during this time.

For the Flames, that's Nemec, whom they acquired from the Devils in the offseason. He could end up being a core piece of this roster and a power-play quarterback, but he's going to struggle as he takes on big minutes on a bad team.

Carolina Hurricanes: I Smell Back-To-Back Cups

The only significant roster change for the Hurricanes is the loss of goalie Freddie Andersen, who signed a one-year deal with the Oilers in free agency.

Could the Hurricanes win the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes? If anyone could pull that off, it would be GM Eric Tulsky. Hellebuyck's got leverage, and if his buddies are any indication, he probably has his heart set on an American contender.

The Hurricanes have the cap space — and the open space in the net — to pull it off. If that happens, why wouldn't the Hurricanes be prime two-peat candidates?

Chicago Blackhawks: Bowen Byram Pops Off

The Blackhawks have been highly criticized for the price they paid for Byram in their trade with the Sabres, and the criticism is fair.

They surrendered their No. 4 overall pick and more to acquire a player who had 11 goals and 42 points in 82 games last season. Plus, they took this gigantic swing on a defenseman when they're still looking for the right winger to complement Bedard.

That being said, Byram is a great young player with tons of potential and was an important part of the Sabers' resurgence. This could actually work out.

Colorado Avalanche: They'll Make it to the Final

The Avalanche were the most dominant team in the NHL last season, and they almost extended all the way to the Cup Final.

Cale Makar and Nathan MacKinnon, two of the biggest stars in the league, both got injured beyond recognition just in time for the Western Conference Finals. That's the risk you take when two of your players make up so much of your production, and we're seeing between the Panthers and the Hurricanes that depth is the name of the modern Cup winner.

Both are young enough and hungry enough for one more run, though. With Makar becoming the richest player in NHL history, this year's a perfect year to return to the Cup Final.

Columbus Blue Jackets: Jet Greaves Establishes Himself As An Elite Goalie

The Blue Jackets had a mess of a summer, and Zach Werenski and Kirill Marchenko playing chicken will no doubt impact the team's vibes. Between that situation and RFA Adam Fantilli still holding out unsigned, it seems doubtful the Blue Jackets will return to the playoff bubble this season.

Despite all of that, they've found their goalie in Jet Greaves. The 25-year-old keeps improving, keeps putting up elite underlying numbers, and has held down the fort through the ups and downs with this team as of late.

This is the year he transitions from "impressive up-and-comer" to "elite NHL goalie."

Dallas Stars: They've Peaked as a Really Good Team

The Stars are a masterclass in how to be consistently great in the NHL over a sustained period. We all measure success in different ways, and it's a success in itself that this team has been in the contender conversation for so long and has kept things interesting for the fans.

There's some bad luck working against them, with the Avalanche and the Wild providing the most brutal path to the Cup of arguably all time. Sometimes, you can do everything right and you still just can't reach the end goal. Such is life.

Detroit Red Wings: Dylan Larkin Stays The Course

Dylan Larkin had a highly-memeble press conference at the start of Red Wings training camp.

You'll recall he was stripped of his captaincy after requesting a trade out of Detroit. Since requesting that trade, though, Steve Yzerman stepped down (what are we calling it?) as GM, and the next GM has yet to be named.

When he was asked about all of this at his aforementioned press conference, he said he "was not ready to go there yet."

Pure speculation, here, but I think he isn't ready to go there yet because he is holding out hope for a new GM.

Edmonton Oilers: Desperation Doesn't Pay Off

The Oilers have made a laundry list of decisions as drastic as they've been unpopular this offseason. Obviously, this is all an attempt to throw everything at the wall and see what sticks in the last season of Connor McDavid's bridge deal.

The trouble is, they were already one game away from winning the Cup Final twice. They didn't need to change that much to get there. Freddie Andersen in net, a healthy Leon Draisaitl, and a healthy Zach Hyman likely would've sufficed.

They're trying too hard, and it won't pay off.

Florida Panthers: This Won't Be a Walk in the Park

Look, I think the Panthers will make it back to the playoffs this season. The reasons they missed out last season were plentiful: Their most important players were seriously injured, the rest of the team was suffering from back-to-back Cup exhaustion, and Paul Maurice knew better than to have the team exhaust itself further and just shut it down to recover for the upcoming season.

They're going to be back and ready to compete this season, but they're also getting older, and they're without star goalie Sergei Bobrovsky. The Atlantic is brutal, and it won't be a walk in the park for the Panthers to make it back into the playoffs.

Please free us from the shackles of LA Kings playoff hockey. The slow, miserable death they suffered at the hands of the Avalanche in the first round last season was so brutal that I almost forgot they got swept.

It lasted forever. I hated every second of it. And didn't we all see it coming?

Quinn Hughes wants to win. The Wild are in a position to do so in a few years, when the Avalanche have nowhere else to go but down. Wild GM Bill Guerin is known to invest in key players. The Devils, where Hughes would otherwise end up to play with his brothers, feel a bit lost right now.

My sense is that Hughes will extend in Minnesota. Does that mean he'll stay for the duration of the contract? Who knows. But I see him with the Wild for the next few seasons as he chases a Cup.

Montreal Canadiens: Lane Hutson for Norris

So many elite puck-movers have emerged in the modern NHL that we can't pay attention to all of them at once. I hope you've been keeping tabs on the rise of Lane Hutson, which coincides with the Canadiens' rise for a reason.

The 22-year-old now has two wildly impressive seasons under his belt. Last season, he averaged 23:46 minutes per game, while putting up 12 goals and 78 points in 82 games. He's been a pivotal part of Montreal's success, and he's just getting started.

Nashville Predators: They Won't Be A Complete Dumpster Fire!

You know it's been a rough couple of years when the idea that your team isn't a complete dumpster fire is a bold take.

But with GM Chris MacFarland, we trust, and he's already righting the ship with offseason moves like bringing Ross Colton and Jack Drury from his former team, the Avalanche, into the fold, plus trading for Mavrik Bourque and Ilya Lyubushkin from Dallas.

New Jersey Devils: It's Time For A Coaching Change

The Devils have needed a bit of new blood all around in management and staff, and they took the first step by hiring GM Sunny Mehta. They've gotta keep shaking things up to get out of a stale situation, so it might be time to look at bench boss Sheldon Keefe and see what else is out there in the coaching market to make the most of Jack Hughes' prime.

New York Islanders: One More Season of Disappointment Before Glory

The Islanders have their long-term superstar in Matthew Schaefer, and he had a wonderful rookie season, seamlessly transitioning to the NHL. His work in the top defenseman role was enough for the Islanders to enter the playoff conversation a few times last season, but they ultimately fell short.

They haven't done much to improve their roster ever since, and the competition out East is only getting stiffer. The Islanders have to build on the sturdy foundation of Schaefer and Ilya Sorokin to take the next step.

New York Rangers: They're Back In The Playoff Conversation

The Rangers made a ton of savvy moves this offseason, and it felt like the beginning of the end of a painful cycle.

They managed to sign Vegas top scorer Pavel Dorofeyev, which will provide a much-needed boost to their production. Oliver Bjorkstrand will help round things out on both ends of the ice. Plus, it could be time for 21-year-old Gabe Perreault to have his big breakout year. There's much to pay attention to with the Rangers early on this season.

Ottawa Senators: They're Out of the Playoff Conversation -- For Now

The Senators got dealt a rough hand this offseason. Not only did they lose their captain and team cornerstone, but his leverage in the negotiations left them with limited options for a return.

Losing a point-per-game player while you were just establishing yourself as a playoff team is a tough blow. The Senators will get over the loss of Brady Tkachuk, but it's going to take a season or two of stocking up on replacements.

Philadelphia Flyers: They're Not Done, But Last Season Wasn't A True Representation of This Team

Sometimes there's a huge benefit to being an extremely young NHL team with emerging talent: You don't know what you don't know. The Flyers' first playoff run with this core had a dash of that, as the roster overperformed all the way to the second round, where the Cup winners swept 'em.

They've improved their goaltending situation with Dan Vladar stepping up and Joseph Woll now in the fold, but they still need center depth and a few other positional upgrades.

But hey, Porter Martone is Porter Martone. We aren't counting this team out of the playoffs just yet, but a step back before a step forward wouldn't be surprising.

Pittsburgh Penguins: One More Run For Crosby

It's probably Alex Ovechkin's last year in the NHL, and while we'll likely still get a few more years of watching Sidney Crosby, this feels like the end of their era of dominance.

Penguins GM Kyle Dubas has delicately balanced the roster to remain competitive while Crosby is still leading the team, while also preparing for his twilight years. This feels like the best chance Crosby and the Penguins have got for one more special season with The Kid.

The Sharks made some great moves this offseason as they flirted with playoff contention last season. They took a jump to 34 points in the standings in 2025-26, and it feels like it's only up from here after Macklin Celebrini's breakout season, in which he led the Olympics in scoring with 45 goals and 115 points in 82 games.

Given the Pacific's weakness, the Sharks' playoff run feels inevitable this season as Celebrini rises to household-name status.

Seattle Kraken: A Rebuild Would Be Smart at this Point

The Kraken are lost in the no-man's-land between having a well-structured team with sound depth and a constant lack of top performers who can elevate play and provide the production needed to thrive in the modern NHL.

Where do they go from here? Do they keep hoping Matty Beniers or Shane Wright suddenly breaks out and becomes that guy, or do they cut their losses and draft another "that guy"?

The Blues have long been in purgatory, but a series of moves over the past few seasons has made next season intriguing.

Mason McTavish has got tons of potential, and just as much to prove. Dylan Holloway's offer sheet continues to pay off. This could be a gigantic year for Robert Thomas as he establishes himself as the team's leader. There's a sense that this team is climbing out of the middle, and that's a heck of a lot better than standing still.

Tampa Bay Lightning: They'll Be Annoying As Ever

Oh, you thought the Tampa Bay Lightning were finally going to leave us alone? Silly you!

Nikita Kucherov is showing no signs of slowing down and has a new contract with a potentially huge payout. The rest of the team is essentially intact, with John Carlson in the fold.

Jon Cooper and the Lightning are going to be just fine, yet again.

Toronto Maple Leafs: This is Going to Take a Second

Are you expecting the Leafs to magically return to the playoffs after a down season so drastic that they ended up drafting No. 1 overall pick Gavin McKenna? Not so fast.

This team is coming into a new identity, post-Marner and entering McKenna's first year.

Sergei Bobrovsky adds an interesting element in net, but the new home is still an adjustment. There are a lot of adjustments going on here, and that's OK. Just don't expect a quick playoff run, and you won't be disappointed.

Utah Mammoth: Logan Cooley Hits Point-Per-Game Status

Logan Cooley was on a special run in 2025-26 until a devastating, untimely injury sidelined him. He managed 19 goals and 43 points in 54 games, after a 2024-25 season featuring 25 goals and 65 points in 75 games.

He's going to come back motivated, and he'll hit the points-per-game milestone if he stays healthy.

Vancouver Canucks: Marco Rossi Turns Things Around

It was obviously a bummer that the Canucks had no choice but to trade their franchise cornerstone, Quinn Hughes. But when they got Marco Rossi in the deal, it was one of the first times in a long time you thought to yourself, "Hmm, not a bad situation for the Canucks."

This season, we'll see him flourish into the No. 1 center role the Canucks have long needed an upgrade at.

Vegas Golden Knights: Mitch Marner Hits 100 Points

Marner has enjoyed great success in his new home. He had a historic postseason breakout, leading the entire league in scoring with 29 points in 22 games. He scored a natural hat trick in Game 3 of the SCF, the fastest playoff hat trick in finals history, in 6:10.

Where will he go from here? Consider that the Golden Knights are without top scorer Dorofeyev. Marner and Vegas' other top players are going to have to contribute even more, and I think Marner is up to the task.

With a year of acclimation and a stellar postseason under his belt, Marner could make some noise in the Hart Trophy race next season.

Washington Capitals: They're Back In The Playoffs

The Capitals narrowly missed the playoffs last season with a record that would've punched a ticket in the West. Classic Eastern Conference mayhem.

Now, Alex Ovechkin is back with the help of Alex Tuch and Jordan Kyrou, and the team is on a mission to give Ovechkin one last run. With Logan Thompson in net, they'll be back.

We'll have to see what the Connor Hellebuyck situation becomes, right? We're all patiently waiting as GM Kevin Cheveldayoff seeks the best return for the world's best goalie.

Once that dust settles, it's time to take a long look at management and staff. This team has not performed up to its potential year after year, and things are taking an even worse turn with Hellebuyck wanting out and last season's missed playoffs.

Is it time to put Cheveldayoff on the hot seat?

articles.title: Who is Matt Lawrence? Meet former FA Cup finalist captain who came back from the dead twice after fentanyl overdoses

articles.body: Matt Lawrence, the former Millwall captain who played in the 2004 FA Cup final, has spoken publicly about surviving two near-fatal drug overdoses in New York in March 2021. Lawrence said cocaine he bought was laced with fentanyl, causing him to stop breathing on two occasions within four days. He was revived both times.Now 52, Lawrence has been sober since August 2025 and is sharing his story for the first time. He spent 16 years as a professional footballer, with his career including spells at Wycombe Wanderers, Fulham, Millwall, Crystal Palace and Gillingham. He later moved to the United States.Who is Matt Lawrence?Matt Lawrence is a former English professional footballer who played primarily in defence. His career included six years at Millwall, where he became captain and helped the club reach its first FA Cup final in 2004.Millwall faced Manchester United at the Millennium Stadium that year. Lawrence walked out as captain alongside Roy Keane. Manchester United won 3-0, with Cristiano Ronaldo among the scorers.After retiring from football, Lawrence struggled with alcohol and cocaine addiction.His most serious episodes happened in New York in March 2021. On March 17, he took cocaine that had been contaminated with fentanyl. He collapsed in Manhattan and stopped breathing.Emergency responders administered Narcan, the brand name for naloxone, which reverses the effects of opioids. Lawrence was taken to hospital and survived.Four days later, another overdose nearly killed him. He had taken more cocaine from the same batch. This time, he collapsed inside a bar and stopped breathing again. A priest reportedly gave him the last rites.Lawrence described how his addiction had changed his view of the danger.“It’s scary how I came to normalise everything. Normalised buying drugs, which is illegal. Normalised being an angry person because that’s what drugs do. They make you snappy and argumentative. I managed to normalise dying because I came out of hospital and didn’t stop. I normalised dying twice in the space of four days”, Lawrence told Daily Mail Sport.He later returned to cocaine despite surviving the overdoses. He said he fell back into drug use within six months and his intake became worse.“I fell back into it within six months, and fell back even deeper. I didn’t die again but my drug intake and frequency got worse. I regret all of that. What it did to me financially, what it did to me domestically and what it did to me professionally. I thought I was living my life and getting away with it, but I was out of control”, he said.“I was incredibly depressed. Spending days in tears doing drugs and days in tears not doing drugs. Miserable and upset. My girlfriend and I sat across the dinner table last August, and she just said: ‘You have to stop, you can’t do this anymore’I am sober as we speak today, I’ll be sober for the rest of today and tomorrow”, he continued.August 10, 2025 became Lawrence’s first day of sobriety. articles.title: Ex-WWE Champ Jack Swagger Injury Update Revealed by Dana White After Emergency Eye Surgery
articles.summary: Former WWE and AEW star Jake "Jack Swagger" Hager underwent surgery following his loss to Johnny Magna at Slap Fight 23 last Thursday.
articles.body:
Former WWE and AEW star Jake "Jack Swagger" Hager underwent surgery following his loss to Johnny Magna at Slap Fight 23 last Thursday.

Speaking to reporters after Tuesday night's Dana White's Contender Series MMA event, UFC president and Slap Fighter co-founder Dana White provided an update on Hager and the eye injury he suffered.

"He went into emergency surgery that night, and then we're sending him to a specialist down in Miami," White said.

Hager, 44, is best known for his pro wrestling career, which spanned from 2006 to 2025.

After starring at the University of Oklahoma in wrestling and football, Hager signed a developmental deal with WWE in 2006 and started going by the name Jack Swagger.

He made is main roster debut in 2008 and went on to become a one-time world heavyweight champion, ECW champion and United States champion, as well as a Money in the Bank ladder match winner.

After departing WWE in 2017, he began an MMA career in Bellator and also signed with AEW in 2019.

Hager went 3-0 with one no contest in four Bellator bouts from 2019 to 2020, and during his AEW tenure from 2019 to 2024, he was most notably part of the Chris Jericho-led stables known as The Inner Circle and The Jericho Appreciation Society.

After announcing his retirement from pro wrestling last year, Hager made his Power Slap debut by beating Devin Jenkins at Power Slap 19 in April 2026.

Hager has since lost a pair of Power Slap bouts against Magna and Amanpreet Singh, who goes by the name Mahabali Shera as a pro wrestler.

articles.title: Asian Games: One fight separates Roshibina Devi from wushu gold medal
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Naorem Roshibina Devi is one victory away from rewriting Indian wushu history.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Naorem Roshibina Devi is one victory away from rewriting Indian wushu history. Already the country’s most successful wushu athlete at the Asian Games — the Manipuri has gone from bronze at Jakarta 2018 to silver at Hangzhou 2023. Now, with another silver medal assured in Aichi-Nagoya, she has the chance to change its colour and become the country’s first Asian Games wushu gold medallist.The 25-year-old stormed into the women’s 60kg sanda final on Wednesday, defeating Indonesia’s Thania Kusumaningtyas 2-0 at the Aichi Prefectural Martial Arts Hall. Roshibina will face China’s Zhang Xiaoyu in the final on Thursday, with history within touching distance.Her route to the final has been emphatic. She opened her campaign by beating Bangladesh’s Shika Khatun in the pre-quarterfinals before producing a 5-0 victory over Macau’s Chu Man Sin in the quarterfinals. The semifinal against Thania brought another controlled performance, taking Roshibina through to her third Games medal.What makes the run more remarkable is that Roshibina was not even the original choice for the continental event. She lost to teammate Divyanshi Choudhary in the selection trials in Srinagar in June. Divyanshi was initially picked but was later ruled out after an MRI revealed a high-grade ACL tear. The Wushu Association of India (WAI) then brought Roshibina back into the squad.Divyanshi alleged mental harassment and preferential treatment by the federation to draft in Roshibina. Amid the raging issue, Divyanshi threatened suicide before retracting. articles.title: Players Championship 30: Karel Sedlacek wins first PDC Pro Tour title as furious Scott Williams throws darts on the ground after loss
articles.summary: Karel Sedlacek became the first player from the Czech Republic to win a PDC Pro Tour title, after he beat Scott Williams in the final of the Players Championship 30; watch the World Grand Prix from September 28, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
It was a thrilling encounter, with Sedlacek outlasting Williams' barrage of high scores, which included nine maximums, but both players struggled to close out the victory, with the Czech missing five match darts.

Sedlacek would ultimately claim victory, becoming the first Czech player to win a PDC tour title. But after mounting an epic comeback, winning two of the final three legs, Williams cut a furious figure after the match, shaking hands with his opponent and the officials before throwing his darts onto the ground.

Sedlacek would go 7-5 up before nerves set in, with the 47-year-old needing to check out on 24 to win, before missing a trio of match darts, allowing Williams to pull back a leg.

The momentum turned to Williams, who hit two 140s in the resulting leg, before he pulled the contest back to 7-7.

In the deciding leg, it looked as though the Englishman was set to produce a remarkable comeback victory, hitting a maximum to leave himself 112 to win the match, but he too stumbled, hitting five on his second dart when a single 20 would have double 16.

Williams shook his head and exclaimed, 'you're kidding me', before hitting 15 with his final dart.

It left Sedlacek the chance to check out from 32, first missing double 16 inside, subsequently missing double eight, before he finally sealed the match.

Sedlacek, who hit a match-high checkout of 164 in the ninth leg, finished the final with a checkout success of 34.8 per cent, while Williams ended with 36.8 per cent.

"It's a really special achievement," Sedlacek told PDC TV . "I've been waiting for this for nearly 10 years, and now it is a reality.

Sedlacek, who lauded his opponent Williams as a "good player" after the match, booked his spot in the final by beating some top opponents, including Damon Heta in the round of 32, Nathan Aspinall in the last 16 and Chris Dobey in the quarter-final, before besting Niels Zonneveld 7-2 in the semi-finals.

"It means everything," he said. "I've played for more than 30 years and now I've done it. I'm at the top of my career now and I'm really happy.

"I'm feeling stronger and I know I can play darts but I need more matches. But this is perfect.

"Darts is growing day by day in Czech Republic. More players and good players are coming through, this is one of the best points of my career and every player in Czech Republic will hopefully say, 'Karel has done it, we can do it too!'"

articles.title: Luke Littler: Does world champion need to change approach to hostile crowds after whistling at World Series of Darts Finals?
articles.summary: Luke Littler's treatment by the crowd at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam overshadowed the world champion's failure to deliver on stage; watch Littler's World Grand Prix defence live on Sky Sports from September 28
articles.body:
Littler's bid for a clean sweep of all major PDC titles in 2026 was ended on Sunday after a crushing 10-4 defeat to Jonny Clayton in the last eight at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam, but the action was overshadowed by the Brit's unhappiness at being repeatedly whistled at by the Dutch crowd.

After facing significant hostility during his win over home favourite Danny Noppert on Friday, Littler threatened to boycott future tournaments in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled at during his victory over Nathan Aspinall on Saturday, prompting referee Charlie Corstorphine to intervene.

Littler has taken a stance against volatile crowds before, refusing to travel to European Tour events in Germany as a result of his treatment from fans there.

On the latest episode of the Love The Darts Podcast, World Series of Darts Finals champion Ross Smith explained his own approach to hostile crowds, which he admits is inspired by three-time world champion Michael van Gerwen.

"It's a real difficult situation," Smith said. "I can't speak for Luke because I'm not him and I wasn't in his position, I wasn't on stage at the time. I didn't really experience the whistling too much. I try not to rise to it because I know you're just going to get more stick.

"My manager once said to me, if you look at Michael van Gerwen, he never reacts, not once will he ever react to the crowd. He'll always thank them and he never really gets too much stick and he's very professional about how he does things. So, I admire him for that and I try and learn off of other people.

"I had a bit with Kevin Doets, obviously the crowd, rightly so, they're cheering their local guy on. Same with Gian [van Veen], they're doing exactly the same, but I think if you're aggressive towards the crowd and you're letting them know that it's affecting you and you're making them unhappy, it's not a good thing.

"I tried to, with Gian, I had more banter with them, you know what I mean? Just like thumbs up to them, but smiling, not in an aggressive way and they sort of laugh with you, it's not a problem.

"I think it's how you can react on stage, if you're aggressive towards them, it's going to create problems for you. But like I said, I can't really comment on Luke because I wasn't playing in the games with Luke and I don't know what he actually went through, but they can be brutal at times."

Nicholson: Maybe Littler can learn from others

Former world championship quarter-finalist Paul Nicholson praised Smith's approach, and suggested that Littler could benefit from learning from some of his rivals.

Nicholson, who himself was known for often having fractious interactions with crowds, also pointed to the way 2021 world champion Gerwyn Price has adapted his behaviour on stage.

Following on from Smith's comments, Nicholson said: "That's a really, really good way of looking at it, what Ross has just said, because from my standpoint, I tried to be aggressive because I wanted to be different and it was something that I had my entire career for, more than 10 years.

"Gerwyn Price has taken years to figure it out. Now he gives the smile with the aggression, and the crowd are with him more than they ever have been.

"So, it just goes to show that Ross is looking at this right, in order to make sure that his career is in the right place moving forward.

"So, we learn from mistakes, but we actually learn from what other people are going through as well. We don't want to see Littler not going to events, but maybe he can learn from what other people are doing as well."

Why whistling is worse than booing for players

Nicholson also explained why Littler and other players may become particularly frustrated at being whistled.

He added: "We have seen Littler have some banter with the crowd, which we're all for by the way, because we want people to have that connection. One of the greatest things about this sport is that there is a connection between the fans and the stars.

"But what we have at the minute is a trend of people using whistling as a way to make themselves feel heard. Dart players don't like it because it's piercing. It gets in your ear and it happens in a very short, sharp way, and it comes from nowhere.

"You don't know if it's going to come when you're throwing a match dart, a leg dart, or even going for a treble. If it comes out of nowhere, it can put you off and your shoulder jolts, and you don't want that.

"A boo is a lesser frequency and it's more mundane, you can handle them a lot better. But these short, sharp whistles, which is what they are, they're horrible.

"And the worst thing is, if it happens once, you are thinking about whether it's going to happen again, and you can't fully focus."

articles.title: UFC's Mackenzie Dern Teases WWE Future, Oba Says 'F--k You' to Bronson, AEW Rumors on Young Bucks
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe and All Elite Wrestling.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe and All Elite Wrestling.

UFC's Dern Interested in Future WWE Career

Mackenzie Dern is enjoying enormous success as a UFC fighter, but a future foray into pro wrestling with WWE is on her radar.

Speaking recently to Daniel Trainor and Mike Vulpo of Us Weekly , Dern expressed interest in entering the squared circle one day with WWE.

"Oh yeah, that'd be fun. So much fun," Dern said. "I mean, the Bella [Twins]. It's so cool. I'd be able to once I retire."

In addition to her affinity for a pair of WWE Hall of Famers in Nikki and Brie Bella, Dern mentioned former UFC and WWE star Ronda Rousey as someone she would like to face before her MMA career is over, saying, "Ronda Rousey is a lot bigger, but it would have been amazing to do like an exhibition match with her."

If Dern does eventually make the leap to WWE, she will be following in the footsteps of Rousey, who established herself as the biggest women's MMA star of all time before going to WWE and becoming a multi-time women's champion.

While not necessarily as dominant as Rousey was in the Octagon during her heyday, the 33-year-old Dern has enjoyed a remarkable career, compiling a 17-5 record.

That includes beating Virna Jandiroba last year at UFC 321 to win the vacant UFC women's strawweight title.

Dern successfully defended the title against Gillian Robertson in August, and she remains the reigning UFC women's strawweight champ.

That suggests Dern's UFC career isn't ending any time soon, but when it does, it sounds like she is heavily considering WWE.

WWE Releases Video of Oba/Reed Interaction

After trading blows once again during Monday night's episode of Raw, WWE released a video of a tense interaction between Oba Femi and Bronson Reed.

Femi saved Je'Von Evans from a potential three-on-one beatdown at the hands of The Vision, which resulted in Oba and Bronson getting some big shots in on each other.

Oba prevented Reed from hitting him with a steel chair and ultimately sent Reed out of the ring with a massive chair shot to his back.

Femi had some choice words for Reed following the physicality, and WWE transcribed The Ruler's verbal barbs in a video on X, as he told Reed, "Get out of here! You and me. You and men. Mano a mano. You step on my face, f--k you!"

Oba was seemingly referencing a previous interaction between himself and Reed, which made some waves throughout the wrestling world.

During the Sept. 7 episode of Raw, Femi was left laying in the middle of the ring thanks to an attack at the hands of The Vision.

While The Vision admired and celebrated their handiwork, Reed placed his foot on top of a prone Femi, only for Oba to swipe Reed's foot away.

Following that, WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t Cain A. Knight of Cageside Seats) reported that Oba's actions were not part of the script, and some people in WWE weren't fans of him going into business for himself in that moment.

Despite that, WWE is clearly still moving forward with Femi vs. Reed and The Vision as a whole, and Monday's interaction suggests WWE is leaning into the controversy that surrounded their previous encounter.

Rumored Details on The Young Bucks' AEW Contracts

The Young Bucks have been central figures in AEW since its initial creation, but they reportedly could be in line to hit free agency in the near future if they choose to do so.

Speaking this week on his Talk'n Shop podcast (h/t Felix Upton of Ringside News), former WWE, NJPW and TNA, and current MLW star Karl Anderson commented on The Young Bucks' contractual status:

Anderson said he talks to Matt and Nick Jackson "every single day," and noted that their AEW deals are set to expire some time in 2027.

He went on to admit that he has no idea how much longer The Young Bucks intend on wrestling.

While there were various points over the years where it felt like a possibility that The Young Bucks would make the leap to WWE, it is somewhat difficult to envision it happening at this point.

Matt and Nick are executive vice presidents of AEW, giving them far more skin in the game with AEW than a typical wrestler.

There is likely no scenario in which they would be given that level of power and responsibility upon signing with WWE, so re-signing with AEW feels like the obvious resolution.

Of course, nothing is impossible in pro wrestling, as Cody Rhodes decided to return to WWE despite being an AEW EVP in his own right.

Unlike Rhodes, The Young Bucks were never part of WWE in the past, though, which makes them leaving AEW feel far less realistic.

articles.title: 2 Chicago Bears on PUP list return to practice — but not Kyler Gordon — while Case Keenum gets QB1 reps
articles.summary: The major news for the Chicago Bears on Wednesday is who isn’t on the practice field — backup quarterback Tyson Bagent — but two players will practice for th...
articles.body:
The major news for the Chicago Bears on Wednesday is who isn't on the practice field — backup quarterback Tyson Bagent — but two players will practice for the first time this season.

The Bears opened the 21-day return-to-practice window for defensive end Shemar Turner and linebacker Noah Sewell to return from the reserve/physically unable to perform (PUP) list. That means they will be on the practice field for the first time since being injured last season.

Case Keenum will be the No. 1 quarterback during practice as starter Caleb Williams (hamstring) and Bagent (concussion) will not participate when the Bears begin preparing for Monday night's game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Soldier Field. Coach Ben Johnson said Williams was present for the morning walk-through but Bagent is not at Halas Hall as part of the NFL's concussion protocol.

"We're at a point right now, not sure who the starter is going to be on Monday night," Johnson said before practice. "We'll let this thing play out and we'll go from there.

"One of those things that everyone outside the building I am sure is writing us off and telling us it can't be done, and we really relish that. So guys will step up to the plate, guys that maybe we don't anticipate or expect."

Johnson had said Monday that he didn't anticipate Williams practicing this week, but he stopped short of ruling him out for the Week 3 game. Bagent has to be cleared from the concussion protocol before he's an option.

Defensive reinforcements could be available soon, provided Turner and Sewell respond well. The soonest players who began the season on the PUP list can return to the 53-man roster is Week 5.

The Bears did not open the practice window for nickel cornerback Kyler Gordon , who has been sidelined all year with a calf injury. Gordon has been away from the team while rehabilitating, and although social media videos have surfaced of him working out, Johnson didn't have any details to share about his status.

Asked if there have been encouraging signs for Gordon in recent weeks, Johnson replied, "I've got nothing to add there."

Turner, a second-round draft pick last year, has been recovering from a torn ACL suffered in the Week 8 loss in Baltimore last season. The Bears initially used him on the interior before sliding him outside to defensive end, where they believe he can be strong against the run.

Turner and Dominique Robinson combined for a huge tackle of Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty for a 3-yard loss inside the red zone midway through the fourth quarter of the Week 4 game last season. The Raiders were forced to kick a field goal, keeping it a one-score game, and the Bears eventually won on D'Andre Swift's 2-yard touchdown run followed by Josh Blackwell 's blocked field goal.

Sewell suffered a torn Achilles tendon in the Week 17 loss at San Francisco . He played in 13 games with nine starts last year and had 59 tackles, one forced fumble and three tackles for a loss while also being a core contributor on special teams. How he would fit in on defense when he's on the 53-man roster remains to be seen. D'Marco Jackson has served as the third linebacker in the base package through two games.

The Bears could have some moving parts in the secondary Monday. Cornerback Tyrique Stevenson is week to week with a hamstring injury. That could lead them to move rookie Malik Muhammad II outside with veteran Cam Lewis assuming Muhammad's duties in the slot.

articles.title: NC State QB CJ Bailey takes a positive approach in moving forward after costly Vanderbilt fumble
articles.summary: CJ Bailey figured he had a choice in how he responded to making the mistake that turned N.C. State's road win into one of the most improbable losses in colle...
articles.body:
RALEIGH, N.C. (AP) — CJ Bailey figured he had a choice in how he responded to making the mistake that turned N.C. State's road win into one of the most improbable losses in college football in years .

The quarterback could brood over that devastating moment. Or he could focus on moving forward for Saturday's visit from Appalachian State .

"The last several days have been good," Bailey said after practice Wednesday, four days after losing a fumble in the end zone that Vanderbilt recovered for a last-second touchdown. "A lot of guys have my back, Coach (Dave) Doeren, everybody in the facility.

"They've been leaning on me, I've been showing up. I've been waking up on the right side of the bed every morning, feeling good."

It marked the first time the third-year starter had spoken to reporters since the loss, which came after N.C. State (1-2) led 31-28 and faced a fourth-and-3 play from its own 5-yard line with 6 seconds left. Doeren said Monday the call was for Bailey to burn time before going down to take a safety, leaving Vanderbilt hoping for nothing short of a miracle with nearly no time left.

Bailey had space to take a knee or scramble out of the back of the end zone. Instead, he started running toward the oncoming desperation pass rush, then took a hit that knocked the ball loose for Vanderbilt's winning recovery in a shocking moment.

Bailey said he "just was trying to get all the clock out."

"The biggest thing was just hold the ball, bro," he said. "That was the biggest thing. I was just trying to run around and make a play, being competitive. That's who I am, I'm a competitive guy. I was just competing to the final second and it happens. I fumbled the ball, I'm going to kick myself up and keep going."

Offensive lineman Teague Andersen was one of the first teammates to reach Bailey in the end zone and help him up. Andersen said Bailey was "pretty distraught" afterward.

Still, Andersen said Wednesday, he offered his QB an immediate message: "Dude, no matter what happens, bro, I've got your back."

That kind of support carries Bailey now. Bailey said his mother is in town and made some home-cooked meals. He said he's heard words of encouragement from outside the program, too.

The list included former Wolfpack passing great and longtime NFL star Philip Rivers , as well as Peyton and Eli Manning , team spokeswoman Annabelle Myers said. Bailey previously attended the Manning Passing Academy, an annual camp attracting some of the nation's top college QBs.

Bailey patiently fielded questions Wednesday with an almost happy-go-lucky demeanor, pointing to optimism from how the team has practiced. He said he had addressed teammates with a key message.

"I just said: 'We've got a long season,'" Bailey said, "'we've got so many more games and so many more plays that we can make.'"

articles.title: Spain advances to Billie Jean King Cup semifinals against Czechia by beating Kazakhstan 2-1
articles.summary: Spain advanced to the Billie Jean King Cup semifinals for the first time in 18 years by clinching a 2-1 win over Kazakhstan in the decisive doubles match whi...
articles.body:
SHENZHEN, China (AP) — Spain advanced to the Billie Jean King Cup semifinals for the first time in 18 years by clinching a 2-1 win over Kazakhstan in the decisive doubles match while saving 18 break points Wednesday.

Cristina Bucsa and Sara Sorribes Tormo allowed just two of the 20 break chances they faced in a 6-2, 7-5 win over Anna Danilina and Zhibek Kulambayeva.

On Friday, Spain will face Czechia, formerly known as the Czech Republic, which brought Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova and Marie Bouzková to Shenzhen.

The Czechs beat Britain 2-0 on Tuesday to stay on course for a 12th title in the competition previously called Fed Cup. The United States, which did not qualify for the finals, won a record 18 titles.

Spain won it five times in the 1990s and last reached the final in 2008.

Jessica Bouzas Maneiro gave Spain a lead Wednesday, beating Sonja Zhiyenbayeva 6-2, 6-2, then Kazakhstan leveled with Yulia Putintseva's 6-2, 3-6, 6-1 win over Bucsa.

The other two quarterfinals matches are on Thursday: two-time defending champion Italy faces China; and Ukraine plays Belgium.

articles.title: Malago: ‘Italy must look to present and future, we’re all in the same boat’
articles.summary: FIGC President Giovanni Malagò reassured the Italy squad that they are ‘all in the same boat’ focused on the present and the future, while there is ‘good new...
articles.body:
FIGC President Giovanni Malagò reassured the Italy squad that they are 'all in the same boat' focused on the present and the future, while there is 'good news' on the EURO 2032 stadiums.

The chief visited the Coverciano training ground today to see coach Roberto Mancini and the players, many of them getting their first experience of senior international football.

CORTINA D'AMPEZZO, ITALY – MARCH 05: Giovanni Malago, President of the Organising Committee for the 2026 Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games, speaks during the Paralympic Games Opening Press Conference ahead of the Milano Cortina 2026 Winter Paralympic Games at on March 05, 2026 in Cortina d'Ampezzo, Italy. (Photo by Mattia Ozbot/Getty Images)

"I've made these speeches many times in my life, varying of course depending on whether it is a team sport or an individual one," Malagò told reporters.

He was for many years the President of the CONI, the Italian Olympic Committee that oversees all sporting activity in Italy.

"If there's one thing that people recognise me for, it's my ability to connect with athletes and speak to their hearts. I was given the great honour by then-President Gabriele Gravina of being invited to speak to the players when they were preparing for the Euros in 2021, and I hope that helped then too."

FIGC President Giovanni Malago (left) with coach Roberto Mancini (right): @coppa_canottieri via Instagram.

What did he tell the Italy players in today's meeting as they go into the Nations League and have to put the disappointment of World Cup failure behind them?

"I told them we are all in the same boat, not different ones traversing together. I talked about faith, optimism, self-belief. In Sport you don't always achieve the results you want, but it is still important to feel joy.

"Italy is watching us, now more than ever, and we must all show a certain faith."

It was Malagò who brought Mancini in for his second Italy tenure, so how does the FIGC President like the first call-ups?

"I'd be crazy not to. It was pretty much what I expected, considering how the coach thinks, so something consolidated and something with prospects for the future.

"In two years we'll play the Euros, in four a World Cup, results permitting, and in six the Euros at home where at least we've qualified regardless. All jokes aside, we must look to the future over those six years, otherwise it'd be irresponsible, but at the same time look at the present and maybe even what happened yesterday."

October 1 is the deadline for Italy to present the dossier on its six stadiums to co-host EURO 2032 with Turkiye.

"UEFA asked for some extra documentation to the one presented in late July, and I won't reveal anything here, but we have seen some positive news."

For Texas, getting Arch Manning going and comfortable is going to be a major key to the game. Not only is this game on the road, but in front of over 100,000 fans at Neyland Stadium, where his uncle, Peyton Manning , was a star. The Volunteers' defense is giving up just 16.5 points per game and is stellar against the pass. Manning has completed 59 of 96 passes this year for 661 yards and seven touchdowns. He has been sacked four times while throwing two interceptions. Manning has not been running as much either, with just 21 attempts for 93 yards. He needs to find some explosive plays to Cam Coleman as well. Coleman has averaged over 16 yards per reception this year, while scoring four times.

On defense, Texas needs to slow down the running game of Tennessee, which begins with maintaining gap discipline on the option. The Volunteers have the number two running offense in the nation this year while Texas is 32nd against the run. The combination of DeSean Bishop and Daune Morris has been solid out of the backfield. Bishop has run for 286 yards with four scores, while Morris has 234 yards and two touchdowns. Meanwhile, quarterback Faizon Brandon has run for 137 yards and three touchdowns. If Texas can force Tennessee into more passing situations, they may be able to slow down the Tennessee attack.

Meanwhile, Tennessee needs a strong performance from Faizon Brandon. Brandon is a true freshman, and this will be the most difficult defense he has faced. He has completed 41 of 64 passes this year for 552 yards and six touchdowns. He has also run for 137 yards and three touchdowns. The quarterback has yet to throw an interception this year and has been great at keeping the ball out of danger. As long as he can avoid turnovers and not give Texas a short field, Brandon has the skill to keep Tennessee in the game.

On defense, Tennessee needs to force obvious passing situations. The running game for Texas has been solid with Hollywood Smothers and Raleek Brown . Smothers has run for 198 yards and two scores while Brown has run for 129 yards and two touchdowns. The duo has kept the offense ahead of the chains and out of clear passing downs. Further, it has helped Texas control the tempo of the game. They have been holding the ball for over 35 minutes per game so far this year. Further, Tennessee needs to also be careful on the play action to not allow big plays over the top to Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo .

College GameDay will be on site for the contest between Texas and Tennessee as one of the biggest matchups of the week. Both teams have high-tempo and quick-strike offensive units that can score in a hurry. Still, both teams have been great at stopping the run this year, and the Tennessee front seven has been solid at getting pressure even without blitzing. The line being under seven points provides a benefit for Texas, and this is a huge step up in competition for Tennessee. The combination of Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo is going to be difficult for the Tennessee secondary to stop. Texas is going to be able to fluster Faizon Brandon and take the home crowd out of the game early.

Final Texas vs. Tennessee Prediction and Pick: Texas -4.5 (-112) and Under 55.5 (-108)

articles.title: Eli Manning gives nephew Arch advice following Holly Rowe controversy
articles.summary: Here's the advice that Eli gave Arch.
articles.body:
Arch Manning 's status as both the Texas starting quarterback and a Manning puts a spotlight on him, and that got him onto some hot water recently.

Manning was at the center of a controversy involving Texas, Steve Sarkisian and Holly Rowe, as he admitted to laughing at an AI video of Sarkisian slapping Rowe after the Ohio State game. Manning later apologized for his actions, saying it was "insensitive."

"It's easy to say I didn't mean it, but I know my words and actions were hurtful to a lot of people," Manning said. "I do not take that lightly and am deeply sorry for that."

Fortunately for Arch Manning, he has a few uncles he can turn to for advice on how to handle the media. In fact, Eli Manning told Front Office Sports how he would advise his nephew when dealing with the media as a starting quarterback in college and the NFL.

In a conversation with Front Office Sports, Eli Manning said that he tries to keep his advice with Arch more football-related. However, he did have a tip for the younger Manning about how to deal with the media as a star quarterback.

"He'll have to figure out that media on his own, and a lot of it is just kind of growing pains," he said. "You feel like they're your pal, you relax with them a little bit, you try to be funny, and then they can take it and run. So you just gotta be careful, you gotta find your moments where you can be funny, you can be relaxed, but there's certain things that you know you just gotta learn and deal with it. And I think he has learned, and he apologized and did the right steps in handling that."

Eli Manning spent his entire career in the New York spotlight dealing with a tough media environment, so he has plenty of experience knowing how to navigate that part of the job. Arch Manning, meanwhile, is still in just his second season as a starting quarterback and is still learning how to handle himself in front of the media.

Both Eli and Peyton Manning had their own controversies in college, but those occurred before the age of social media. Now, Arch has to be even more careful than his uncles to ensure he doesn't go viral for all the wrong reasons.

articles.title: R Ashwin reveals former IPL-winning Indian coach was in contention to become CSK coach before Zaheer Khan's appointment
articles.summary: Ravichandran Ashwin reveals that before Zaheer Khan was given the go-ahead for the CSK head coach role, a former IPL-winning Indian coach was the frontrunner...
articles.body:
R Ashwin revealed Ashish Nehra was among the names considered for the CSK head coach role.

Two unnamed Indian legends and several foreign candidates were also reportedly in the frame.

Ashwin backed Zaheer Khan's eventual appointment, citing his close relationship with MS Dhoni.

Ashish Nehra was in contention for the role for CSK coach before Zaheer Khan's appointment

Chennai Super Kings' search for a successor to Stephen Fleming was apparently a far more extensive process than the eventual appointment of Zaheer Khan suggested.

R Ashwin, speaking on his YouTube channel, revealed that the franchise held conversations with several candidates before settling on Zaheer, including a fellow former India pacer currently thriving elsewhere in the league.

Fleming departed CSK in July after 18 seasons and five IPL titles, going on to take charge of England's Test team. Zaheer's appointment was confirmed on September 21 on a one-year contract, giving him his first head coach role at franchise level after previous spells as director of cricket for Mumbai Indians and as a mentor at Lucknow Super Giants.

Ashwin, closely associated with CSK across his playing career, suggested the process behind that appointment involved considerably more names than have been publicly reported.

What R Ashwin revealed about Ashish Nehra's candidacy

Ashwin named Nehra as one of the figures discussed for the role. "There have been conversations with several coaches. In fact, if I'm not wrong, I think Ashish Nehra was also at some stage in the frame," Ashwin said.

He was careful to frame Nehra's situation as one of contentment at Gujarat Titans rather than confirming any formal rejection. "Ashish Nehra doesn't need to leave GT. He's running an absolutely successful franchise in GT," Ashwin said .

That framing lines up with Nehra's own record at the franchise. He led Gujarat Titans to the IPL title in their debut season in 2022, becoming the first Indian head coach to win the tournament, and has since guided the side to multiple playoff appearances, including a runners-up finish in 2026.

Ashwin also indicated the search extended well beyond Nehra. "I think there are two other Indian legends whose contracts were also discussed. There were a few foreigners whose contracts were discussed, but the deals couldn't materialise for many reasons," he said, without naming the individuals involved.

He offered some insight into why those foreign discussions stalled. "In some cases, they were not ready to take a one-year contract. In fact, in one case I know well, the deal was almost done, but the issue was that he couldn't work in international tournaments apart from CSK, because of which he could suffer financially," Ashwin said.

Why Ashwin believes Zaheer Khan is the right choice

Despite detailing how extensive the search had been, Ashwin was unequivocal in his support for the eventual outcome. "I think the choice of Zaheer Khan is fabulous. I do not doubt it," Ashwin said. "He ticks all the boxes. Smart man, knows cricket, knows bowling tactics well, and will blend in nicely."

He pointed specifically to Zaheer's relationship with MS Dhoni as a key factor behind the appointment's likely success. "His relationship with Dhoni is very good. Besides, he is an Indian legend who can work with the boys," Ashwin said. "Dhoni and Zaheer Khan's rapport is good. I think you can see the team going in one direction; there won't be a need to pull here and there."

What makes this disclosure notable is less about who CSK didn't hire and more about what it reveals of their process. A franchise willing to explore multiple India greats and international candidates before landing on someone without prior head coaching experience suggests the final call rested heavily on fit and existing relationships rather than pedigree alone.

Given how much weight Ashwin places on the Zaheer-Dhoni dynamic, that appears to have been exactly the deciding factor CSK were looking for.
